target_customer: Young professionals in expensive US cities renting a private room in a managed co-living building
problem: Housing in San Francisco and similar cities is very costly; co-living offers cheaper furnished rooms with shared space.
business_model: Developer and operator of co-living buildings, monthly room rent

founders.name: Jon Dishotsky
founders.background_notes: YC page describes him as entrepreneur turned investor and founding partner of Daft Capital. Joined Common in the 2021 deal.

founders.name: Josh Lehman
founders.background_notes: Cofounder per YC page; later works on Martian Engineering.

founders.name: Jesse Suarez
founders.background_notes: Listed on YC page; no bio.

exit.reason: Management contracts taken over and Starcity brand wound down; Common did not buy land or development assets. Dishotsky said the model was unsustainable in the pandemic downturn (per search summary of trade press).

competitors.name: Common
competitors.what: Co-living startup from the General Assembly founders opening 12 bedroom houses in San Francisco SoMa
competitors.traction_then: Private rooms about 2600 dollars a month; later reported over 2600 applications

competitors.name: WeLive
competitors.what: WeWork residential co-living, opened in New York and Crystal City in 2016
competitors.traction_then: No immediate San Francisco plans in 2016

technical_complexity.rationale: Core work was real estate development and operations plus a resident app, not hard technology.

defensibility.rationale: Buildings and leases were capital intensive but competitors such as Common offered the same product; no network effect or proprietary data was shown.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Common, a direct rival, took over Starcity's management contracts in June 2021 as the sector consolidated.

market_need_then: San Francisco rents were very high and the trade press (Bisnow, SF Chronicle 2016) described co-living filling an affordability gap.

branding.domain_note: Used joinstarcity as an identifier in aggregator listings; actual domain history not found.

identity.visual_style: Boutique hospitality style per press comparisons
identity.voice_and_tone: Community and lifestyle focused; CEO wanted a lifestyle brand residents love (per trade press summary)

branding.brand_signature: Resident app for connecting with neighbors, described as a hyperlocal Nextdoor

brand_strength.rationale: Described by the YC page as one of the largest co-living brands with over 1500 units by early 2021, but the brand was wound down by the acquirer and no source shows fan or viral activity.

outcome_analysis: Starcity grew from a 2016 San Francisco co-living operator to over 1500 units across several cities, raising a 16.45M Series A in 2018 and a 30M Series B in April 2020. The pandemic hit demand for shared housing and the capital intensive development model, and in June 2021 rival Common took over its management contracts and retired the brand. Price is undisclosed. The company had also bought Ollie in 2020, adding complexity before the exit.
